data.run_rule: blank must have no signal in the comparison region
data.origin: synthetic distances; no real botanical chromatogram or solvent procedure

quests.title: Chromatogram investigator: the missing signal
quests.scenario: Two fictional comparable profiles have passed the specified run controls. Determine the largest signal discrepancy and its limited meaning.

Compare each coded peak in a table and trace.

dataset.review_status: design fixture; not scientifically approved for learner release

data.normalization: same internal-reference scaling and dry-material basis; stipulated in this fixture
data.model: fixed vector comparison, not a chemical-composition simulator

correct_reasoning: Peak C differs most: 36−120=−84 units, a 70% decrease relative to its reference value.

The discrepancy warrants investigation but does not independently establish adulteration, identity, a named compound or clinical potency. Sampling, preparation handling, storage and material variability are candidate explanations.

error_feedback.compound_from_letter: A letter labels a signal, not a chemically identified molecule.

transfer_variant.required_conclusion: X is 70% lower; investigate without declaring adulteration. Changed labels/order prevent memorizing Peak C.

quests.scenario: A generic functional-group card and two mathematical response curves are available. Neither curve is a measurement of a plant constituent.

data.functional_group_card: R–OH; R is an unspecified organic group
data.x_units: dimensionless model input; never a human dose

correct_reasoning: R–OH is the generic alcohol cue; it is not a verified structure of a particular plant constituent.
A has a fourfold lower model EC50 than B (2 vs 8) with equal modeled Emax=100. This supports a relative potency statement only within this stipulated model.
The model establishes neither a biological target, real assay effect, clinical efficacy, safety nor administration guidance.

Limits inference to the model and rejects a clinical/dose claim.

quests.title: Evidence belongs to a preparation and an outcome
quests.scenario: Two invented study summaries are being used to market a third, different preparation.
player_actions: Compare design, comparator and exact intervention identity.
Calculate the randomized trial risk difference in percentage points.
Interpret its supplied uncertainty interval and reject an unsupported product transfer.

dataset.review_status: design fixture; not scientifically approved for learner release

studies.analysis: fictional intention-to-treat summary; equal 5% follow-up loss stipulated

data.marketed_product: TRAIN-PREP-B, different composition/route details not supplied
data.endpoint: fictional binary symptom response; not a real botanical outcome
data.interval_method: rounded teaching interval, approximately normal risk-difference interval

correct_reasoning: E2 provides a controlled randomized comparison; E1 cannot by itself separate intervention effects from time, expectation or other changes.

E2 response difference=30%−20%=10 percentage points (RR=1.5 if additionally requested). The supplied interval spans zero: the estimate is imprecise, neither definitive benefit nor demonstrated equivalence.
Neither invented trial establishes a real clinical claim, and evidence for PREP-A does not automatically apply to PREP-B.
rubric_checks: Distinguishes the uncontrolled and randomized designs.
Interprets the interval spanning zero without claiming equivalence.
Rejects transfer to PREP-B without comparability evidence.
Keeps the synthetic study and endpoint separate from real efficacy claims.

error_feedback.percent_vs_points: 30% compared with 20% differs by 10 percentage points, not 10% relative.
error_feedback.no_significance_no_effect: An interval including zero is compatible with multiple effects; it does not prove equivalence.
error_feedback.traditional_equals_trial: A traditional-use assessment and a randomized outcome answer different evidence questions.

transfer_variant.required_conclusion: 4 percentage points, uncertainty spans zero, and applicability to the marketed preparation remains unestablished.

quests.mastery: At least 8/10 across five 0–2 rubric checks; all critical gates passed. Hinted/corrected attempts are practice, not independent mastery. Competency unlock also requires independent transfer evidence.

quests.title: The Mystery of the Herbal Capsules
quests.scenario: Two virtual capsule batches carry the same botanical declaration. Evidence is incomplete and one valid analytical profile differs. The learner submits a qualified research report.
player_actions: Reconcile batch/accession/specimen/material/preparation records.
Inspect authentication and microscopy records, retaining missing evidence.
Check analytical comparability and controls; quantify the discrepant signal.
Separate observations from hypotheses and choose discriminating follow-up tests.
Evaluate a promotional clinical claim for a different preparation.
Submit a structured report, cite evidence IDs and defend the uncertainty statement.

dataset.review_status: design fixture; not scientifically approved for learner release

batches.authentication_record: AR-A checked in the fictional dossier

data.sampling: one virtual aliquot per batch; representativeness not established

correct_reasoning: LOT-B has incomplete authentication/microscopy evidence and a 70% lower coded C signal in a comparable valid synthetic run. These are separate findings.
There is a justified quality concern requiring further work; no particular cause, fraud, adulterant, compound identity, clinical inferiority or whole-batch conformity is established.

Prioritize representative resampling with custody records, authenticated identity/microscopy review and a validated repeat/orthogonal analytical method suited to the question. Investigate storage, supplier documentation and preparation consistency as hypotheses.

The oil-preparation claim does not establish capsule efficacy or safety. The report must explicitly distinguish confirmed dossier facts, model assumptions, missing evidence and unresolved conclusions.
rubric_checks: Run validity, comparability and the −70% C-signal difference are correctly interpreted.
Confirmed findings, missing authentication and sampling limitations are distinguished.
At least two plausible alternative explanations are kept as hypotheses.
Follow-up tests and representative sampling are selected to discriminate hypotheses.
The report qualifies its conclusion and addresses source/preparation applicability and safety limits.

error_feedback.fraud_from_fingerprint: The profile difference raises a question, not a verdict about supplier intent or a named adulterant.
error_feedback.missing_is_negative: A missing microscopy record is not a failed microscopy result.
error_feedback.one_sample_certifies_batch: The dossier does not establish representative sampling.
error_feedback.clinical_from_signal: A coded signal is not evidence of therapeutic potency.

critical_errors: Recommending use/administration of the unknown product.
Declaring a specific adulterant, clinical benefit or causality without evidence.

transfer_variant.required_conclusion: Invalidate the LOT-B run before inferring a batch difference; investigate/retest. Do not merely repeat the taught low-C explanation.

quests.mastery: At least 10/12 across six 0–2 dimensions, no dimension zero, all critical gates passed. Assisted attempts count as practice; competency unlock needs separate independent transfer evidence.
